bullets: clock 2:48-2:34 (t=257-272): the standard opening is split Wall Breakers at centre (8, 14), then Magic Archer behind the king tower at (9, 0), then a Goblin Barrel the moment the opponent commits — pressure first, defence assembled behind it.

clock 2:17-2:03 (t=290-302): the defensive shell is Bomb Tower in the central pocket plus Berserker at the bridge plus Royal Delivery, with the Magic Archer never traded — "This will be a very clean defense." He is willing to let the Bomb Tower die to the Bowler rather than protect it.

clock 1:51-1:17 (t=315-351): in double elixir the deck's engine is Goblin Barrel + Wall Breakers + Fire Spirit in a single rotation, timed off the opponent's cycle ("he's one card off of the barbarian brill"); both enemy towers fell from ~3000/2200 to 580/1788 HP inside forty seconds.

clock 1:03-0:47 (t=363-380): against the Balloon Freeze all-in he stacks Bomb Tower + Magic Archer + Royal Delivery + Ice Spirit before the push arrives — "even if he freezes, yeah, he's not going to take out our tower" — and immediately re-opens with Fire Spirit + Berserker + Wall Breakers.
clock 1:35 (t=332): the deck's win rate against this opponent hinged on spell tracking, not damage — "because he has no [Tornado], he's not going to be able to take out our magic archer."

Match won against the knowledge base's Loon HeroKnight Double Dragon Bowler control deck (Baby Dragon / Balloon / Barbarian Barrel / Bowler / Freeze / Inferno Dragon / Knight Hero / Tornado); Ryley's sign-off at 418-424s: "That was a perfectly played game ... Just a master class right there."

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Ice Spirit and Fire Spirit all demand the same small spell, so whichever the opponent cannot answer connects; the 2.5 average elixir makes it a cycle deck as well.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Three cheap threats — Goblin Barrel, split Wall Breakers and the spirits — each ask for the opponent's small spell, and at 2.5 average elixir the deck comes back around to them faster than the answers do. The defence is a Bomb Tower in the central pocket backed by Royal Delivery and Ice Spirit, which together blank the Balloon Freeze and Bowler pushes this deck's control matchups rely on. The Magic Archer is the piece that makes it more than a chip deck: placed behind the king tower he pierces through a push into the tower behind it, and Ryley treats keeping him alive as the game plan — "make sure that we keep this magic archer completely healthy" (277s), and once the opponent's Tornado is out of cycle he simply leaves him down. Played this way the deck wins by counting the opponent's rotation rather than by out-damaging them: cheap pressure drains the answers, then the barrel and Wall Breakers land in the rotation where none is available.
